name: Khagrachhari
tagline: A green hill district of the Chittagong Hill Tracts — the torchlit Alutila cave, mossy waterfalls and hilltop ponds, Chakma–Marma–Tripura villages, and the road gateway to Sajek.

guide.bestTime: October to March — dry trails, clear hill views and safe cave footing. The monsoon (Jun–Oct) fills Richang Waterfall but makes the rock slippery.
guide.gettingThere: By bus from Chittagong (~3.5–4 hr) or overnight coach from Dhaka (~9–10 hr); there is no railway or airport in the Hill Tracts. Internal travel is by chander gari (open-top jeep), CNG and motorbike. Alutila and Richang are close to town; Dighinala — the road head for Sajek — is ~21 km north.
guide.difficulty: Easy to moderate. Khagrachhari is a Chittagong Hill Tracts district with army/BGB checkpoints; Bangladeshi visitors travel freely to the main sites, while foreign nationals need permission (handled through the DC's office or a registered operator). Rules can tighten without notice — confirm the current situation locally, especially for onward travel toward Sajek.

mustVisit.name: Alutila Cave & Tourism Complex
mustVisit.description: A roughly 350-ft natural cave in the Alutila hills at around 3,000 ft, pitch-dark inside and crossed by torchlight in ten to fifteen minutes, with a hilltop viewpoint complex above. The district's single best-known attraction.
mustVisit.history: Locals call it Matai Hakar — 'cave of the gods' — and it has long been the symbolic gateway to Khagrachhari tourism, now framed by a managed complex and viewpoint.

practical.hours: Daylight; cave entry with a torch/guide
practical.entryFee: Small entry fee; torch hire extra

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 7–8 km west of town on the Khagrachhari–Matiranga road, Sadar/Matiranga

mustVisit.bestTime: October to March — drier, less slippery cave floor
tips: Hire a torch and local guide at the entrance — the cave is fully dark and slick
Wear grippy shoes; the descent to the cave mouth is steep

mustVisit.name: Richang Waterfall
mustVisit.description: A multi-tier cascade dropping over moss-covered rock through dense green hills, with a natural rock slide forming at the base in good flow. One of the more accessible falls in the Hill Tracts.
mustVisit.history: A long-loved local swimming and photography spot near Alutila; the flow is strong only in and just after the monsoon.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 10–11 km from town off the Khagrachhari–Matiranga road, Sadar/Matiranga
howToReach.transport: Chander gari / CNG, then a short walk

mustVisit.bestTime: June to October for full flow; rock is slippery then
tips: The final approach is a steep walk down steps then a dirt trail — go slow on wet rock
Combine with Alutila as one trip

mustVisit.name: Jhulonto Bridge & 'New Zealand', Dighinala
mustVisit.description: A hanging footbridge over the Maini river area at Dighinala, paired with a flat, lush paddy plain that locals nickname 'New Zealand' for its green expanse ringed by hills.
mustVisit.history: Dighinala is the regional town and the road head for onward travel toward Sajek; the bridge and plain are easy, scenic roadside stops on that route.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 21 km north of town, Dighinala Upazila

mustVisit.bestTime: October to February — clear skies over the plain
tips: Easily paired with a Sajek run since both use the Dighinala road
Check the day's checkpoint situation locally before heading on toward Sajek

mustVisit.name: Mayabini Lake, Panchhari
mustVisit.description: A calm hill-ringed lake of clear water with a small island hill at its centre, where visitors row small boats among the forested shores. A quieter, less-commercial alternative to the headline spots.
mustVisit.history: Set at Kanchanchhari in Panchhari upazila, it has grown into a gentle day-trip destination away from the busier Alutila circuit.
mustVisit.bestTime: November to February — still water, good reflections
tips: Boats are available on site for a small fee
Bring your own snacks and water — facilities are limited

mustVisit.name: Hatimura (Hatimatha)
mustVisit.description: A dramatic, very steep hill route — locally Mayang Kapal, around 1,200 ft — with long concrete staircases climbing through forest past a string of Indigenous para (villages). A genuine workout with big views.
mustVisit.history: Increasingly popular for its raw scenery and glimpses of village life along the climb, in Perachhara union of Sadar upazila.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Perachhara union, Khagrachhari Sadar — a drive plus a strenuous walk
howToReach.transport: Chander gari / CNG, then climb on foot

mustVisit.bestTime: October to March — dry, cooler climb
tips: The staircase is long and steep — carry water and start early
A local guide helps with the village trail sections

mustVisit.name: Devata Pukur (Nuya Dhala), Matiranga
mustVisit.description: A large natural pond — about 1,600 ft long — sitting atop a hill at roughly 1,000 ft, reached by a kilometre-long uphill trail from Nunchhari village. Revered locally as the 'Pond of God.'
mustVisit.history: Visited by pilgrims as well as trekkers, it sits in a Tripura village along the Khagrachhari–Rangamati road and carries genuine religious significance.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Nunchhari village off the Khagrachhari–Rangamati road, Matiranga area
howToReach.transport: Chander gari / CNG, then a ~1 km uphill walk

tips: Take a local guide from Nunchhari para
Treat it respectfully — it is a place of worship

specialties.name: Pajon
specialties.description: Khagrachhari's famous mixed hill-vegetable dish, combining many varieties — dozens, by some counts — of greens, ferns, bamboo shoot and herbs, often with a little dried fish.

specialties.name: Bamboo Chicken
specialties.description: Chicken (or fish) stuffed with herbs and slow-cooked inside a green bamboo tube over fire — the signature hill dish, Chakma-style.

specialties.name: Pinon-Hadi Weaving
specialties.description: The traditional handwoven Chakma women's two-piece — the pinon skirt and hadi wrap — made on backstrap looms and prized at hill celebrations.

bucketlist.title: Cross the Alutila cave by torchlight
bucketlist.detail: A ~350-ft natural cave the Tripura call Matai Hakar, 'cave of the gods' — pitch-dark, crossed in ten minutes by torch, with a hilltop viewpoint above.

bucketlist.title: Slide down Richang Waterfall
bucketlist.detail: A mossy multi-tier cascade with a natural rock slide at the base — the most accessible fall near town.

bucketlist.title: Stand on the 'New Zealand' plain at Dighinala
bucketlist.detail: A flat, lush paddy expanse ringed by hills beside a hanging bridge over the Maini — the green that earned its nickname.

bucketlist.title: Row across Mayabini Lake
bucketlist.detail: A still hill lake with an island at its centre in Panchhari — the quiet alternative to the busy spots.

bucketlist.title: Climb the Hatimura staircase
bucketlist.detail: A steep stairway up Mayang Kapal through forest and Indigenous para — a real workout for a big hill view.

bucketlist.title: Hike to Devata Pukur
bucketlist.detail: A 1,600-ft-long pond atop a hill, revered as the 'Pond of God,' reached by a kilometre uphill from Nunchhari.

bucketlist.title: Eat Pajon, the many-vegetable dish
bucketlist.detail: Khagrachhari's famous hill plate — dozens of greens, ferns and bamboo shoot cooked together with a little dried fish.

bucketlist.title: Try Chakma bamboo chicken
bucketlist.detail: Chicken slow-cooked inside a green bamboo tube over fire — smoky, herby, the signature hill dish.

bucketlist.title: Set off for Sajek from Dighinala
bucketlist.detail: Khagrachhari is the road gateway to Sajek Valley — though Sajek itself lies just across the line in Rangamati district.

bucketlist.title: Buy a handwoven pinon-hadi
bucketlist.detail: The Chakma women's two-piece, woven on a backstrap loom in bold patterns — the district's signature textile.

bucketlist.title: Ride a chander gari into the hills
bucketlist.detail: The open-top 4WD jeep is how Khagrachhari moves — grinding up ridges with the valley falling away beside you.

bucketlist.title: Catch the view from Tareng
bucketlist.detail: A hilltop viewpoint over Khagrachhari town and the Chengi valley — an easy sunset spot.

foods.name: Pajon
foods.description: Khagrachhari's famous mixed hill-vegetable dish — dozens of greens, ferns and bamboo shoot cooked together, often with a little dried fish.

foods.name: Bamboo Chicken

didYouKnow: Khagrachhari's most famous site, the Alutila Cave, is called Matai Hakar — 'cave of the gods' — and is explored entirely by torchlight through about 350 ft of darkness.
The district is the seat of the Mong Circle, one of only three traditional hereditary chieftaincies in the entire Chittagong Hill Tracts.
Almost half its people are Indigenous — Chakma, Marma, Tripura and others — making Khagrachhari one of Bangladesh's most multi-ethnic districts.
Khagrachhari is the road gateway to Sajek Valley, Bangladesh's most famous hill resort — even though Sajek itself sits across the boundary in Rangamati district.
Three rivers thread the district: the Chengi (the longest), the Maini and the Feni.
Local cuisine centres on bamboo-tube cooking and Pajon — a single dish that can blend dozens of types of hill vegetable.
